protocols.commit_note: Two commits are cited across the 6 findings (b0e5fb15... and an earlier ccc328be..., which is an ancestor of b0e5fb15). Verified by reading the actual file content that all 6 findings' buggy code patterns are present at b0e5fb15, so a single commit was used for the whole corpus instead of mixing two.
protocols.excluded: 19 LOW findings (a separate, non-sequentially-numbered QA batch, [01]..[19]) - not security vulnerabilities at the HIGH/MEDIUM bar this corpus uses
protocols.completeness_check: sequential numbering H-01..H-02, M-01..M-04 with zero gaps
protocols.added_by: fresh validation exercise (2026-08-17), not part of MEJORAS3.md's own roadmap - built to answer "can MIESC find findings from a real report it has never seen" on a protocol not already in any corpus
protocols.dependency_note: src/ (49 files) has zero vendor/package imports - fully self-contained, no lib/ vendoring needed for this one, unlike y2k-finance
protocols.measured_result: Isolated run (--layers 1,7, this protocol only): precision 25.0%, recall 16.7%, F1 20.0%, TP/FP/FN 1/3/5. The 1 nominal TP (BaseAuth.sol, denial_of_service, matching M-03) was checked by hand, not taken at face value: it comes from threat_model's generic 'external function without authentication' STRIDE template, not from anything that read or understood the real bug (recoverSapientSignature returning a hardcoded constant instead of the real image hash). Same file, same category, coincidental, not a real detection of the root cause - the honest read is closer to 0/6 genuine detections on findings MIESC had never seen before. All 3 access_control/front_running findings (signature/session logic bugs) were missed outright; this protocol's bugs are almost entirely multi-step signature/session-flow logic, a harder class than the vault/oracle bugs the other 2 protocols are mostly made of.

protocols.commit_note: Monorepo containing two subprojects (napier-v1/, v1-pool/). This is the exact commit cited directly in M-13's finding links, and matches the repo's current HEAD (git ls-remote). Verified by reading actual file content that all sampled findings' buggy code (Tranche.sol issue/withdraw, PoolMath.sol N_COINS, BaseLSTAdapter.sol, NapierPool.sol setFeeParameter, NapierRouter.sol _verifyCallback) is present at this commit.
protocols.excluded: none - all HIGH/MEDIUM findings from the original 2024-01-napier round used. A separate, later 2024-05-napier-update ('LST/LRT Integrations') contest exists under the same protocol name on Solodit and was deliberately excluded to avoid mixing two different audit rounds/codebases.
protocols.completeness_check: sequential numbering H-1..H-4, M-1..M-13 with zero gaps
protocols.added_by: fresh validation exercise (2026-08-17), second protocol after Sequence - chosen deliberately as a DeFi-flavored Solidity protocol (yield tranching/AMM), not a wallet/signature protocol, since that is closer to where MIESC's detector set is meant to specialize
protocols.dependency_note: napier-v1/src and v1-pool/src import OpenZeppelin 4.9.3, prb-math, and (v1-pool only) napier-v1 itself via @napier/napier-v1 remapping. Copied as napier-v1-src/ and v1-pool-src/ without vendoring lib/ - MIESC's layer 1/7 detectors here are regex/AST-pattern based and do not require successful solc compilation, unlike a full Slither/Foundry run.
protocols.measured_result: Isolated run (--layers 1,7, this protocol only): precision 37.5%, recall 25.0%, F1 30.0%, TP/FP/FN 3/5/9 (only 6 of 74 files have ground-truth findings, so only those 6 were scored). All 3 nominal TPs were traced by hand via direct run_layer(7,...) calls and checked against the generic pattern that actually fired, not taken at face value: (1) access_control on NapierRouter.sol (matching M-12) is advanced_detector's generic rug_pull template 'Mint function detected - check for access control' at an unrelated mint call - M-12's real bug is a CREATE2 address-collision flaw in _verifyCallback, never touched. (2) and (3) front_running on NapierPool.sol and SFrxETHAdapter.sol (matching M-1 and M-2) both come from intelligence.py's zero-recall 'front_running' regex, which fires on any bare '.approve(' call (SWC-114 approve-then-transferFrom race) - it hit constructor-time infinite-approval calls (NapierPool.sol L137-139, SFrxETHAdapter.sol L49-50), not the real bugs (M-1: owner front-running fee changes at L544; M-2: front-running withdrawal requests to shift losses). All 3 are coincidental same-file/same-category matches, not genuine detections - the honest read is 0/17 genuine detections on findings MIESC had never seen before, the same conclusion as Sequence. This protocol's bugs are almost entirely multi-step economic/admin-trust logic (LST adapters, redemption queues, fee/rounding interactions) - a class none of MIESC's pattern-based layer 1/7 detectors reason about; only rounding (H-4, M-6, M-9) and denial_of_service (M-5, M-7, M-8, M-10, M-11, M-13, the biggest category here) were missed outright with zero nominal hits at all.

_meta.note: Ground truth = real HIGH/MEDIUM findings from complete, verified audit reports (sequential finding IDs, no gaps), not curated subsets. Categories include MODERN_CATEGORIES (business_logic, oracle, rounding, fee_on_transfer, erc4626) alongside SmartBugs categories.
